issues.quote: He does it every year. He tells each person what is wrong with theirs.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that at nine the master made everyone show their watches. It gives no annual routine and no regulating or diagnosing of watches.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as a habitual ritual that establishes the master's habits and expertise with watches, which is a whereabouts-adjacent or background claim the sheet does not support.

issues.quote: Mine was exact. I regulated it myself.
issues.fact: The sheet says only "Mine was exact." Nothing says the witness regulated her own watch.
issues.misreading: The added claim that she personally regulated her watch invents a detail about her relationship to timekeeping that a solver might weigh as significant.

issues.quote: He worked on it for four years. He meant it to strike the first minute of the new century.
issues.fact: The sheet gives no duration for the repeater's making and no intended strike time.
issues.misreading: The four-year duration and the 'first minute of the new century' purpose are hints about timing and the watch's significance that the sheet does not give, so a solver could build an inference on them.

issues.quote: He was not a man who would be late for anything.
issues.fact: The sheet says nothing about the master being punctual or about his habits beyond his mood and state at 10:20.
issues.misreading: This unsupported characterisation of punctuality hints that the master's timing was reliable, which could steer a solver toward trusting or discounting particular clock readings.

issues.quote: It is an old remark between him and the clock. I will not repeat it, Inspector, it is not evidence.
issues.fact: The sheet says only that the master said what he always says about the hall clock, with no statement that the remark is private or non-evidential.
issues.misreading: The added assertion that the remark is 'not evidence' is a characterisation the sheet does not give and may suggest the remark bears on the clock's reliability.
